What we will answer

ISA letters: F flow, T temperature, P pressure, A analysis, X calculated, K sequencer; I indicator, C controller, T transmitter, V valve, S switch (HH/LL trip). AIC-124 holds the O2 purity by moving the KS-140 adsorption step time; PIC-123 holds the O2 buffer V-102 through FIC-125. DOF = degrees of freedom; CSS = cyclic steady state.

Derivation · counting handles

Degrees of freedom: variables minus equations

Before pairing anything: how many things can be set at all?

$N_V,\ N_E$
variables, independent equations at the CSS
–
$N_{DV},\ N_{MV}$
set by the surroundings; set by us
–
$N_{DOF}=N_V-N_E$each free variable needs a value from outside
$N_{DOF}=N_{DV}+N_{MV}$outside means the surroundings or a handle
$\text{loops}\le N_{MV}$one loop uses one handle

CSS: every variable is a cycle average; every inventory repeats each cycle.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Safety, equipment, quality, delivery, then efficiency.
  • AIC-124 is direct acting and moves a step time.
  • Fail positions follow the safe state, not the action.
  • DOF = 34 − 17 = 17 = 6 DV + 11 MV.
  • Eight loops use the eight continuous handles.

Eight loops, one sequencer, separate trips

Trips read their own switches; the dashed orange line is the step-time signal to KS-140.

How the loops were chosen

Six rules applied to this unit

  • Objectives and DOF first, then pairing.
  • Each CV with a direct, one-sign handle.
  • Throughput at the feed; buffers held by their outflow.
  • Fast valve loops absorb the pulses.
  • Safety on separate sensors; valves fail safe.
  • Recipe times stay fixed.

Interactive · model runs, one handle +5 % of span, 45 min

Which handle moves the purity, and at what cost?

The step time moves purity −1.17 % in one direction; the purge only +0.10 % and costs product.

Principle · where each inventory is held

Hold each buffer by what leaves it

The customer valve moved only V-102; that makes it the buffer's handle.

V-100 air

Self-regulating; PIC-103 is only a ceiling, normally shut.

V-102 O2

PIC-123 → FIC-125 → FV-125: the customer gets what is made.

V-103 N2-rich

PIC-133 → PV-133 to the N2 users.

No inventory loop reaches back into the cycle.

Interactive · model runs, customer 190 → 175 Nm³/h, 3 h

V-102 on the feed air makes two slow loops fight

The feed moves purity and production a half cycle later: the set point saw-tooths ~200 Nm³/h.

Interactive · pick a structure

Eleven structures: which ones this unit uses

Single loops form the base; the cascade, the sampled purity loop and the sequencer make this unit's structure.

Interactive · model runs, feed 1800 → 1700 Nm³/h, 90 min

Feedforward to the step time, trimmed by AIC-124

Feedforward rule$t=t_0\,F_0/F$

The rule asks 412 s; the model needs more than 418 s: the trim must finish the job.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Purity on the step time: strong, one-signed.
  • Purge and adsorption pressure stay recipe values.
  • V-102 held by FV-125 (cascade), not by the feed.
  • The purity loop is sampled once per half cycle.
  • Feedforward on the feed helps, but needs trim.

Definition · pid() in the model

Ideal PID in % of span, derivative on PV

$e$
SP − PV (reverse) or PV − SP (direct)
% of span
$K_c$
controller gain
%/%
$T_i,\ T_d$
reset and rate times
s
$I,\ D$
integral and derivative parts of OUT
%
$OUT=K_ce+I+D,\qquad \dfrac{dI}{dt}=\dfrac{K_ce}{T_i},\qquad D=\mp K_cT_d\dfrac{dPV}{dt}$

Bumpless start; anti-windup clamps OUT at 0 and 100 %.

Derivation · a P-only loop after a step

Proportional action alone leaves an offset

Previous slide, $T_i=0$$OUT=K_ce+\text{bias}$
$K$
process gain: ΔPV/ΔOUT, both in % of span
%/%
$\Delta$
set-point or load change, as PV
% of span
$\Delta PV=K\,\Delta OUT=K\,K_c\,e$the bias stays fixed
$e_\infty=\dfrac{\Delta}{1+K_cK}$error left when PV stops moving

FIC-101: K = 0.90, Kc = 0.25: 82 % of the step stays as offset.

Interactive · model runs, FIC-101 set point 1800 → 1700 Nm³/h

More gain, less offset — never none

P-only offset$e_\infty=\Delta/(1+K_cK)$

At the simulator's gain P only leaves 84 Nm³/h of the 100; the formula says 82. PI removes it.

Method · first order plus dead time

Read the step as a difference to an unstepped run

P only needed K; a step test measures it, with τ and θ.

$\tau,\ \theta$
time constant, dead time
s
$t_{28},\ t_{63}$
times to 28.3 % and 63.2 % of the change
s
$G(s)=\dfrac{K\,e^{-\theta s}}{\tau s+1},\quad K=\dfrac{\Delta PV}{\Delta OUT},\quad \tau=1.5(t_{63}-t_{28}),\quad \theta=t_{63}-\tau$

Each PV swings with the cycle: subtract a copy run without the step.

Interactive · model step tests, OUT +5 % in MAN

Fast loops, and one integrating buffer

Flow loops settle in seconds; V-102 has no self-regulation and ramps instead.

Tuning rule · lambda (IMC) PI

Choose the closed-loop time constant λ

Step test$G=Ke^{-\theta s}/(\tau s+1)$
$\lambda$
closed-loop time constant: τ smooth, τ/3 tight
s
$K_i$
ramp rate of an integrating PV
%/s per %
$K_c=\dfrac{\tau}{K(\lambda+\theta)},\quad T_i=\tau$self-regulating
$K_c=\dfrac{2\lambda+\theta}{K_i(\lambda+\theta)^2},\quad T_i=2\lambda+\theta$integrating buffer

Interactive · pick a loop, move λ

Where the simulator's tuning sits on the λ line

FIC-101 runs at λ ≈ 4.4 τ (gentle); AIC-124 at λ ≈ 0.26 τ, the tight end.

Interactive · model run, AIC-124 OUT +5 % (step +10 s), 4 h

The purity loop: sampled, with a long lag

The made purity steps every half cycle; AT-124 lags by the buffer: τ 46 min, θ 22 min, so Ti 3600 s.

Interactive · PI on the fitted integrator (θ neglected)

A loose buffer loop is slow and lightly damped

PI on an integrator$\zeta=\tfrac12\sqrt{K_cK_iT_i},\ \ \omega_n=\sqrt{K_cK_i/T_i}$

Simulator 1.5 / 600 s: ζ ≈ 0.26, period ≈ 121 min — loose on purpose, so the customer flow stays steady.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • P only leaves Δ/(1 + KcK); PI removes it.
  • On a cyclic plant, a step test is a difference of two runs.
  • Lambda: Kc = τ/[K(λ + θ)], Ti = τ.
  • AIC-124: τ 46 min, θ 22 min, Ti 3600 s.
  • PIC-123 is loose on purpose: ζ ≈ 0.26.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Rank the objectives, then count the degrees of freedom.

2

Pair purity with the step time: direct, strong and one-signed.

3

Hold each buffer with its outflow, never by reaching back to the feed.

4

Read step tests as differences to a run without the step.

5

Tune slow loops for steadiness, fast flow loops for speed.
